chunks: From him, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“The mukātab is flogged in proportion to the amount of him that has been emancipated,” and he mentioned “that he is flogged with part of the whip, and he is not flogged with its entirety.”

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: has been emancipated; has been freed
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: a slave under a manumission contract seeking freedom through payment
key_terms.بِبَعْضِ السَّوْطِ: with part of the whip; in a limited manner
key_terms.عَلَى قَدْرِ: in proportion to; according to the measured extent
key_terms.كُلِّهِ: its entirety; the whole of it
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: is to be flogged; the prescribed corporal punishment is administered

ai.seo_question: How is the legal punishment of a mukātab determined in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the punishment of a mukātab, linking the penalty to the degree of emancipation attained. It also specifies a limitation in how the flogging is carried out, indicating measured application within the prescribed legal framework.
